name: Azerbaijan
tagline: Fire that comes out of the ground, a walled medieval city, and oil money spent on architecture.
summary: Azerbaijan sits on the Caspian, on gas reserves that have been burning at the surface for millennia — the Zoroastrian fire temples were built around them. Baku pairs a walled old city with a skyline of flame-shaped towers. Beyond the capital the Greater Caucasus rises to 4,000 metres with mountain villages that kept their own languages, and mud volcanoes cover the semi-desert south.

season.note: Spring and autumn; Baku is hot and windy in summer and the mountains are best from June to September. Novruz in March is the biggest holiday of the year.

getting_around: A modern railway links Baku to Ganja and Sheki. Buses and shared taxis cover the rest. Mountain villages like Xinaliq need a 4x4. The Armenian border is closed.
food: Plov, in dozens of versions, cooked in a pastry crust for feasts
Dolma and kebab, argued over with every neighbour
Tea from a pear-shaped armudu glass, with jam rather than sugar
know: The border with Armenia is closed; an Armenian stamp can complicate entry.
Baku's old city and the Gobustan petroglyphs are both UNESCO-listed.
Tea houses are a social institution and usually male-dominated outside the capital.

regions.name: Baku & the Caspian
regions.summary: The walled city, the flame towers, the fire temple and the petroglyphs south of town.

cities.name: Baku
cities.summary: A UNESCO-listed walled city with a mysterious stone tower, ringed by oil-boom mansions and three flame-shaped skyscrapers.
highlights: Icherisheher, the walled old city, and the Maiden Tower nobody can fully explain
The Heydar Aliyev Centre, Zaha Hadid's curved white building
Ateshgah, the fire temple, and Yanar Dag, a hillside that has burned for centuries
Gobustan's 6,000 petroglyphs and the mud volcanoes beside them

experiences.name: Petroglyphs and mud volcanoes
experiences.summary: Rock carvings of boats and dancers from 10,000 years ago, then a field of cold mud volcanoes burping methane a few kilometres on.

regions.name: The Northwest & the Mountains
regions.summary: Sheki's caravanserai and stained glass, and villages high in the Greater Caucasus.

cities.name: Sheki
cities.summary: A silk road town under wooded mountains, with a khan's summer palace whose windows are built without glue or nails.
highlights: The Palace of Sheki Khans, with shebeke lattice windows of 5,000 pieces each
Sheki halva, layered and made only here

experiences.name: Shebeke: glass without glue
experiences.summary: Wooden lattice and coloured glass assembled entirely by friction; the workshops still make them and will show you the joints.

cities.name: Xınalıq
cities.summary: A village at 2,300 metres whose people speak a language related to nothing else, reached by a single mountain road.
highlights: Flat-roofed stone houses stacked up the slope
The Ketsh language, spoken by a few thousand people and nobody else
Shepherd routes into the high Caucasus
